ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A unicycle-riding acrobat performs on a tightrope in the air. The total mass of the acrobat and the unicycle is $\mathbf{m}$, and the two sides of the tightrope form an angle of $2\theta$. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$.

1. Determine the magnitude of the tension in the steel cable.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A unicycle-riding acrobat performs on a tightrope in the air. The total mass of the acrobat and the unicycle is $\mathbf{m}$, and the two sides of the tightrope form an angle of $2\theta$. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$. 1. Determine the magnitude of the tension in the steel cable.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the acrobat is riding a unicycle at the downward sag in the middle of the steel cable; the steel cable extends from that point respectively upward to the left and upward to the right to the supports on the two sides, forming an approximately symmetrical V shape. Reasoning: Treat the acrobat, the unicycle, and the contact point as a stationary force body. The forces include the vertically downward gravity mg, and the equal-magnitude tensions T along the respective directions of the left and right sections of the steel cable. The problem says that the angle between the steel cables on the two sides is 2θ; by symmetry, the direction of the tension in each section of the steel cable makes an angle θ with the vertical direction. Therefore the vertical component of each tension is T cosθ, and the horizontal components cancel each other. Equilibrium in the vertical direction gives 2T cosθ = mg, solving gives T = mg/(2 cosθ).
